context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor and provides case management for fraud analysts. It operates on AWS (`eu-west-1`) to meet PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while respecting strict budget and team constraints.

## Key Elements
* **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System**: Core software system processing authorizations and managing cases.
* **Payment Gateway / Acquirer**: External system sending authorization requests.
* **Fraud Analyst**: User reviewing suspicious transactions.
* **Card Networks & Fraud Intelligence Feeds**: External systems providing risk signals and blacklists.
* **Archival / Compliance Storage**: External AWS S3 and KMS services for 7-year auditability.

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway -> Fraud Screening System via HTTPS / gRPC for real-time scoring.
* Fraud Analyst -> Fraud Screening System via HTTPS (TLS 1.3) for case management.
* Fraud Screening System -> Archival Storage via AWS SDK (TLS) for WORM audit logs.
* Fraud Screening System -> AWS Compliance/Security Services via HTTPS for KMS envelope encryption.

## Technology Stack
* **AWS (`eu-west-1`)**: Cloud provider hosting managed services within a €25,000/month budget.
* **AWS S3 with Object Lock**: Provides tamper-evident, write-once-read-many (WORM) storage for 7-year audit retention.
* **AWS KMS**: Handles card data tokenization and envelope encryption to ensure analysts never see full card numbers.
* **gRPC / HTTPS**: Protocols ensuring decision latency below 50 ms at P99 under 3,000 req/sec.

## Rationale
This architecture offloads operational overhead of PCI-DSS compliance and auditability to AWS managed services, enabling a three-engineer team to maintain the system securely. Using high-performance protocols and managed AWS primitives ensures strict performance, availability, and strict compliance targets are met within budget.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage suspicious cases. It delivers sub-50ms decisions at 3,000 TPS while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (User)
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer (External System)
- Card Networks & Fraud Intelligence Feeds (External System)
- Archival / Compliance Storage (External System)
- AWS Network Load Balancer (Ingress)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Container)
- Case Management Backend (Container)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (Data Tier)
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS (Audit Tier)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway calls AWS Network Load Balancer via HTTPS/TCP at 3,000 TPS.
- AWS Network Load Balancer routes requests to Fraud Scoring Engine via TCP.
- Fraud Scoring Engine queries Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Redis via TCP.
- Fraud Analyst accesses Case Management Backend via HTTPS.
- Case Management Backend reads/writes to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL via TCP.
- Fraud Scoring Engine and Case Management Backend stream audit logs to Amazon S3 via AWS SDK.

## Technology Stack
- AWS Network Load Balancer: Low-latency ingress routing without API Gateway overhead.
- Go or Rust: High-performance backend language to guarantee P99 latency below 50 ms.
- Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate: Container orchestration minimizing operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- Redis: In-memory store for low-latency feature lookup.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational database for transactional case management data.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS: Immutable, tamper-evident storage for 7-year compliance audit logs.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages managed AWS services to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team while staying within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. High-performance containers and load balancing meet the strict sub-50ms latency requirement at 3,000 TPS.

## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and provides case management tools for analysts. It ensures high-performance, compliant, and auditable payment processing on AWS.

* Payment Gateway / Acquirer and Fraud Analyst (Users/External Systems)
* AWS Network Load Balancer (AWS NLB) and Application Load Balancer (AWS ALB)
* Fraud Scoring Engine (Go/Rust on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
* Case Management Backend (Go/Rust on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)

This architecture meets PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints and sub-50ms latency requirements by using direct L4/L7 load balancing and memory-efficient microservices. * API Handler Component (Go / Fiber)
* Feature Aggregator Component (Go)
* Scoring Engine Core (Rust)
* Audit Logger Component (Go)
* Rule & Model Loader Component (Rust)
* Redis
* Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS

* Feature Aggregator -> Scoring Engine Core [In-process Function Call]
* Scoring Engine Core -> Audit Logger [Channel / Async Queue]
* Rule & Model Loader -> Scoring Engine Core [In-process Shared Memory / Atomic Swap]
* Feature Aggregator -> Redis [TCP]

* Rust: Chosen for CPU-bound scoring to meet strict performance and memory safety constraints.

This architecture combines Go for efficient I/O processing and Rust for high-speed, memory-safe scoring to easily achieve the P99 latency target below 50 ms. Utilizing managed AWS services within a modular component structure ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and zero-downtime model updates within budget.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and provides case management tools for fraud analysts. It operates on AWS to meet strict performance, compliance, and auditability requirements.

## Key Elements
- **Case Management Schema**: PostgreSQL tables storing analyst reviews and case states.
- **Audit Log Vault**: `pg_audit` extension and append-only tables capturing immutable decision logs.
- **Row-Level Security (RLS) Enforcer**: PostgreSQL RLS policies enforcing PCI-DSS data segregation.
- **Data Masking & Tokenization Engine**: PostgreSQL functions and `pgcrypto` dynamically masking primary account numbers (PANs).

## Relationships
- Case Management Backend -> Case Management Schema: Reads and writes case data [SQL/TCP]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Audit Log Vault: Appends immutable decision logs [SQL/TCP]
- Case Management Schema -> Data Masking & Tokenization Engine: Sanitizes card data on read [PL/pgSQL]

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL**: Relational database providing transactional persistence and multi-AZ availability.
- **`pg_audit` & Append-Only Tables**: Ensures tamper-evident auditability for 7-year retention requirements (R-06).
- **PostgreSQL RLS Policies & `pgcrypto`**: Enforces strict PCI-DSS compliance and card data tokenization at the database layer (R-05).

## Rationale
This component architecture leverages native PostgreSQL extensions to satisfy stringent PCI-DSS and tamper-evident audit requirements without adding operational complexity for a three-person engineering team. Keeping security and audit controls inside the database layer minimizes code-level compliance drift while maintaining the required P99 performance under budget.

Redis.analysis:
## Overview
The Redis container provides ultra-low-latency feature lookups and sliding-window velocity metrics for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency and automated failover within AWS.

## Key Elements
* **Redis Primary Node**: Amazon ElastiCache instance handling real-time feature writes and fast reads.
* **Redis Replica Node**: Amazon ElastiCache instance providing automatic failover.
* **In-Memory Feature Cache Store**: Redis Hashes and Sorted Sets storing sliding-window velocity metrics using tokenized identifiers.

## Relationships
* **Fraud Scoring Engine -> Redis Primary**: Fetches features and executes Lua scripts for atomic rate-limiting and feature retrieval via RESP protocol [TCP].
* **Redis Primary -> Redis Replica**: Synchronizes state via asynchronous replication [RESP protocol via TCP].

## Technology Stack
* **Amazon ElastiCache (Redis OSS)**: Managed service chosen to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team.
* **Redis RESP Protocol / TCP**: High-performance network protocol ensuring decision latency remains below 50 ms at P99.
* **AWS KMS**: Provides encryption-at-rest for PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.
* **TLS**: Ensures encryption-in-transit across private VPC subnets.

## Rationale
This architecture meets strict performance and availability constraints by utilizing fully managed in-memory replication. It guarantees compliance and security requirements while remaining operable by a small engineering team within a fixed budget.

Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at scale while providing analysts a secure case management interface. It ensures low-latency scoring, 7-year tamper-evident auditability, and PCI-DSS compliance on AWS.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- Card Networks & Fraud Intelligence Feeds
- Amazon NLB (Network Load Balancer)
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go / Rust, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Go / Rust, Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate)
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
- Redis
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock and AWS KMS
  - S3 Bucket (Compliance Audit Store)
  - Key Management Service (Audit Encryption Key)
  - S3 Lifecycle Component
  - Bucket Policy & Access Controller
- Fraud Analyst

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> Amazon NLB: Forwards payment authorization requests [HTTPS / REST]
- Amazon NLB -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Routes authorization payloads [gRPC / TCP]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Redis: Performs ultra-low latency feature lookups [RESP / TCP]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads rules and writes scoring states [PostgreSQL wire protocol / TLS]
- Case Management Backend -> Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Manages analyst cases and reviews [PostgreSQL wire protocol / TLS]
- Fraud Analyst -> Case Management Backend: Reviews suspicious payments and updates cases [HTTPS / REST]
- Fraud Scoring Engine & Case Management Backend -> S3 Bucket (Compliance Audit Store): Writes immutable audit logs [HTTPS / AWS SDK via S3 Gateway VPC Endpoint]
- S3 Bucket -> Key Management Service (Audit Encryption Key): Encrypts/Decrypts payloads [AWS internal API via AWS KMS VPC Endpoint]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Fargate & Amazon ECS: Container execution for stateless scoring and case management, minimizing operational overhead for a 3-engineer team.
- Go / Rust: High-performance languages chosen to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 requests per second.
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational database for persistent case management and fraud rules storage.
- Redis: In-memory datastore for fast feature retrieval during real-time transaction scoring.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock & AWS KMS: Immutable storage utilizing compliance mode and KMS envelope encryption to satisfy 7-year tamper-evident auditability.
- Amazon S3 Glacier: Cost-optimization tier for long-term audit log retention to stay within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict sub-50ms performance and PCI-DSS compliance requirements through serverless containerization and high-throughput memory stores. It controls operational costs via automated storage tiering while guaranteeing tamper-evident 7-year auditability.
